## Fixed

- `model` on a set that draws each storey twice and titles its sheets as
  wrapped headings (corpus dossier 15) built ten storeys, two of them at
  −7.92 and four at −3.96, missed the ground and third floors, and capped
  the house with the template's 7.2 m roof under a third floor at +7.92. It now
  builds the five storeys the plans name (−7.92, −3.96, ±0, +3.96, +7.92) and
  a roof at 11.88:
  - consecutive plan sheets at one titled level are one storey (the
    dimensioned and the furnished sheet);
  - a storey whose title names a level no higher than the one drawn before it,
    between two that climb, is a misprint and stands between them (the set
    titles its second floor `-3,960`, its basement's level);
  - a roof plan that names no level, over storeys whose template roof would
    cut the top one, stands a storey above it.
- Sheet headings: a name wrapped over stacked lines is read as one, with a
  millimetre level before «նիշ» (`7920 նիշում` → 7.92); a level mark followed by
  another number on its baseline (`-0,000 0250`) is read; text placed far off
  the page no longer joins a title line. Dossier 15's pages 14, 15, 18 and 19
  now report `floor_plan` with `certain` confidence (they were
  `cadastral_plan` and `unknown`); no other corpus page changed.

## Scorecard

`model` 0.3750 → 0.4375 (dossier 13 0 → 0.5); every other kind held. Dossier
15's ledger corrected against its pages: pages 14/15 print «Առաջին հարկի
հատակագիծ ±0,000», 18/19 «Երրորդ հարկի հատակագիծ 7920», so their class is
`floor_plan`, and its storey model states the five storeys the plan titles name
(the per-storey areas had been seeded from a run and never reviewed).
